## WHAT THIS CODELINE ACTUALLY IS

`mock-a` is a very small TypeScript library. It has no framework, no server process, no DOM, no
router, no database and no network calls. The entire tree outside `node_modules` is: `package.json`,
`tsconfig.json`, one directory `src/` holding the TypeScript module(s) under test, and one directory
`test/` holding their vitest suite. There is nothing else to find. Two or three `explore` calls plus
`show` on the whole file is a COMPLETE survey here, not a shortcut — read the file end to end rather
than sampling it, because it is short enough that skimming buys you nothing and costs you accuracy.

Conventions this code follows, which your prescription must match:
- ESM only (`"type": "module"`). Relative imports are written WITHOUT a file extension
  (e.g. `from '../src/fares'`), resolved by `"moduleResolution": "bundler"`. Do not prescribe
  `.js` suffixes; do not prescribe `require`.
- `"strict": true`, `target`/`module` ES2022. Exported types are inline `type` aliases, not
  interfaces or classes.
- Behaviour lives in small exported pure functions that take a plain object and return a number or
  primitive. Tunable values are exported `const` UPPER_SNAKE_CASE module constants, and the tests
  assert against those constants by name rather than against literals. If your fix changes which
  constant a branch selects, say which constant — do not write the numeric value in its place.
- Two-space indent, semicolons, single-quoted strings in tests, single-line `if (cond) return x;`
  bodies with no braces. When you copy a `brokenLine`, copy that exact shape.

Commands this project runs (from the repo root):
- `npm test` → `vitest run`
- `npm run build` → `tsc --noEmit` (type-check only; nothing is emitted)
- `npm run lint` → `echo no-lint-configured` — a deliberate no-op. A green lint proves NOTHING here;
  never cite it as evidence.

Because there is no server and no browser in this codeline, "runsIn" for ordinary library and test
modules is `"n/a"`. Do not write `"server"` or `"browser"` for a pure function that is only ever
called by another function in `src/` or by a vitest spec — that is a false claim about where code
executes. Reserve `"server"`/`"browser"`/`"both"` for the case where you have actually SEEN a runtime
boundary in the tool output.

`test/` is inside the `tsconfig` `include`, and the vitest suite is the ONLY caller of the module(s)
in `src/`. So `callers <Symbol>` will usually show you test call sites and nothing more — that is the
real shape of the graph, not a gap in the index. A test file may legitimately be one of your fix
sites; when it is, get `changeRequired` right (true only if that file's own text must change).

SAY WHAT EACH CHANGE DOES TO THE VALUE — "deliveryRole" is REQUIRED, and it is the field this
prompt exists to get right. Exactly one of:

  "produces"  this change is what makes the new or corrected value EXIST. It reads it, fetches
              it, queries it, computes it, or changes configuration so that an existing call
              starts returning it. If you removed only this change, the value would never come
              into being.
  "carries"   this change moves, stores, re-renders or re-exposes a value that something ELSE
              produced, or it subscribes to a signal saying the value changed. Reacting to a

  "verifies"  this change does nothing to the value; the file only needs confirming once the

A PLAN IN WHICH NOTHING PRODUCES IS NOT A PLAN. If every site you name carries or verifies, you
have described the delivery of a value nobody obtains, and the implementation will do visibly
nothing while looking correct — a subscription firing, state updating, a view re-rendering, and
the same stale value on the screen. Before you answer, find the site that PRODUCES. If the
capability genuinely needs no new value, say so in "reason"; if you cannot find where the value
would come from, say THAT rather than naming a carrier and hoping.

In a pure-function codeline the producer is the function whose OWN return value is different after
your edit — the branch, comparison or expression that decides what comes back. A caller that
aggregates, sums, re-exports or forwards those results CARRIES; it will change what a user sees, but
it obtains nothing, and naming only it means nothing was fixed. A vitest spec never produces: it is
`verifies` when it already covers the corrected behaviour, and at most `carries` when it must be
extended to assert the new boundary case.

SAY WHERE EACH CHANGE RUNS — "runsIn" is REQUIRED. One of "server", "browser", "both", "n/a".
An API that only exists in one of those cannot be called from the other, and a prescription that
puts it in the wrong place cannot be implemented at all: the implementer either fails or quietly
does something different. Check what the surrounding function is — an entry point that runs
before a response is sent is not the same place as code running after it is displayed. If a
change subscribes to something, subscribing usually runs where the events happen; obtaining the
value may run somewhere else, and those are then TWO sites, not one.

A consumer that reads state from a provider you are fixing is the usual case. This is not a lesser finding and must not be dropped — a downstream gate requires a real diff in every site you mark true, so marking a verify-only file true makes the story impossible to complete: the implementer changes nothing (correctly), the gate rejects it, and every retry repeats. Saying it in the "fix" prose is not enough; nothing reads prose.
